title: Container image scanning and minimal base images

videos.script: Scan the image linkbox has shipped since lesson one, and the scanner reports three thousand four hundred and eighty-four vulnerabilities. {{count}} Nobody can fix that list. Not one of the Debian findings has a fixed version yet. So a number that size tells you nothing about what to do on Monday. {{nofix}} This lesson reads the report by its columns instead. What the scanner actually read. Which findings a rebuild can fix. Which ones are the same advisory, counted four times. {{columns}} Then it changes the base. Two stages: one that has pip and builds, one that only runs. The image drops from one point six gigabytes to a hundred megabytes, and the scan from thousands to the floor of the base. {{stages}} Last, the pipeline gets two new stages. One scans every image it builds, and breaks the build for what can be fixed. The other pushes the image to a registry on your machine, where lesson ten's cluster will find it. {{registry}} And you will see the gate refuse the old image, on a branch, for four findings in pip. {{refuse}}
